NISER Bhubaneswar UM-DAE CEBS Mumbai

The National Entrance Screening Test (NEST) is a compulsory online computer-based test for admission to the five-year Integrated MSc programme offered by the National Institute of Science Education and Research (NISER) and the University of Mumbai - Department of Atomic Energy Centre for Excellence in Basic Sciences (UM-DAE CEBS). NISER and UM-DAE CEBS are autonomous institutions established by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), Government of India, in 2007. These institutes were started with the mandate of providing research-oriented teaching in basic sciences by faculties of practising scientists aimed at creating a national pool of human resources to lead the nation to excellence in teaching and research in basic and applied sciences.
NEST 2026 will be conducted in around 387 cities across India.

The candidates admitted to the Integrated MSc program are eligible to receive an annual scholarship of ₹60,000 through the DISHA program of the Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India. In addition, the scholarship recipients receive a grant of ₹20,000/- per annum for summer internships. Candidates selected by DST for the INSPIRE-SHE program are endorsed for the INSPIRE scholarship by NISER and UM-DAE CEBS. A vast majority of students graduating from the integrated MSc programs offered in the two institutes pursue doctoral research at universities and institutions of repute in India and abroad, including NISER or CEBS and join academia or industry primarily in research positions. The placements of the graduated students from NISER and UM-DAE CEBS provide testimony to the success of this program.

NISER, Bhubaneswar and UM-DAE CEBS, Mumbai are in compliance with the UGC and Govt. of India guidelines on anti-ragging. Ragging in any form is a punishable offense and hence is totally prohibited on these campuses. Any complaint regarding ragging can be made at the 24x7 toll-free National Anti-Ragging Help Line number 1800-180-5522 and/or at the email-ID helpline@antiragging.in

NISER, established by the Department of Atomic Energy, strives to become a citadel for basic sciences and allied subjects in terms of teaching and research. Its vision includes imparting high-quality science education in a vibrant academic ambience to the bright, motivated students, by a faculty of distinguished scientists and teachers. The curriculum is amply supported by a strong visitors’ programme by accomplished scientists from India and abroad.

NISER offers a 5-year Integrated M.Sc. programme in Biological, Chemical, Mathematical and Physical sciences. Apart from a major in any of these subjects, a student has a choice of a minor in Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics or, Physics. NISER, located near Bhubaneswar in Odisha, is an off-campus centre of the Homi Bhabha National Institute (HBNI), a deemed-to-be university established by DAE. Academic programs of NISER are affiliated with HBNI.

There are a total of 200 seats this year, which include reserved seats for SC/ST/OBC/Divyangjan candidates as per Government norms. 02 supernumerary seats are reserved for eligible candidates from J&K and Ladakh. If offered admission under the OBC-NCL category, the candidate must produce the relevant valid certificate on the date of admission. Further details about the institute are available on the NISER website www.niser.ac.in . Fee structure for integrated MSc programme at NISER can be found here: Fee Structure

The Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India, has an autonomous Centre for Excellence in Basic Sciences in Mumbai. CEBS offers high quality teaching embedded in a vibrant post-graduate and research environment with some of the best teachers and scientists from major institutions in the city (TIFR, BARC, IIT) and the University of Mumbai and its colleges, as its faculty. The Centre is located in the Vidyanagari campus of the University of Mumbai. CEBS offers a 5 year integrated M.Sc. programme in Biological, Chemical, Mathematical and Physical sciences. The degrees at CEBS are awarded by the 150-year old University of Mumbai.

Tentatively, there are 57 seats this year with reservations as per government norms. 02 supernumerary seats are reserved for eligible candidates from J&K and Ladakh. Further details including maximum number of seats in any stream and allotment procedure are on the CEBS website www.cbs.ac.in .

Eligibility Criteria FOR ADMISSION
Candidates must qualify all FOUR eligibility criteria listed below:
Candidates should have at least three out of the four disciplines of basic sciences, namely, Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics, in classes XI and XII.

Candidates should have passed the class XII examination from any recognised Board in India in the year 2024 or 2025 or should be appearing for the same in 2026 . The (provisional) certificate declaring the aggregate should be from a single board. Candidates appearing for the board examination in 2026 must satisfy the eligibility criteria at the time of admission into the programme.

Candidates must secure at least 60% marks in aggregate or equivalent grade in class XII examination. For candidates belonging to scheduled castes (SC), scheduled tribes (ST), and Divyangjan categories, the minimum requirement of marks is 55% in aggregate or equivalent grade in class XII examination.
Candidate should secure a rank in the NEST 2026 merit list.
There is no upper age limit for appearing in the NEST 2026 examination and admission to either NISER or UM-DAE CEBS provided all the above eligibility criteria are fulfilled.

To apply for NEST 2026, candidates must fill out the online application form linked from www.nestexam.in website only. The online application process closes on April 06, 2026 (11:30 pm) unless extended for some reason [See Important Dates ].

Phase - 1: Candidates need to REGISTER themselves first before applying online. During this process some basic information like Name, DoB, eMail-ID, Mobile#, Class X Roll# have to be entered. Provide name and DoB strictly as per certificate. These details cannot be modified. The process sends login credentials via eMail within 30 minutes (max).

Phase - 2: One can LOGIN and proceed to application only after receiving the credentials. Additionally, Forgot Password and Change Password options are there. On successful login, one can click "Go to Application" (on top-right) and provide the required details. Application can be filled partially and saved to be completed later before final submission. Copy (and keep) the Order-ID shown on the very first page of BillDesk to use while raising a complaint for failed payment .

Phase - 3: Seeking technical support is generally not needed if everything goes well. If needed, the query/complaint should first be raised by clicking HELPDESK after login. A suitable problem type has to be chosen from drop-down list and a brief description has to be provided. Screenshot of error page / unsuccessful payment can be uploaded. Alternatively, the tech.support can be contacted over phone.

Syllabus for NEST 2026

The syllabus for NEST 2026 primarily follows the CBSE curriculum (2025-26) and NCERT books of classes XI-XII for Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology. The knowledge gained in the science subjects up to class 10 may also be required to answer some of the questions.
NCERT textbooks can be downloaded directly from https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
Prescribed books are merely suggestive to cover the listed syllabus for NEST 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions
How can I edit a submitted application?
After the closure of application, a window of 1-2 days is allowed to make the correction. (see Important Dates regarding correction window).
Edit Window will be LIVE only for Candidates whose application status is "Payment Success".
Except for Mobile Number, Email ID, Category, PwD details and Test-City Preferences , everything else can be edited . Document update will also be allowed.
Note: The edit window shall be open only for Payment Success candidates.
How can I download my hall ticket?
Login in the application portal with your application number (N26xxxxxx), password and captcha. Hall ticket download link is visible only if the application is complete in all respects.
Candidates are advised to carefully verify all details mentioned in the hall ticket after downloading.
What should I do if I am unable to download the hall ticket/admit card?
Admit card will not be sent via post/email.
You have to download it from this webpage (http://www.nestexam.in/) by logging in using your registration#/ application#/ user-id and password.
And check your network connectivity, clear your browser cache, enter the correct captcha and try again.
If still unsuccessful, contact the helpdesk indicated on the NEST webpage as below.
Priority-1 # Use grievance portal - click 'Helpdesk' after Login.
I found an error in my name/photo details on the admit card. How can I get it corrected?

After the admit card has been generated, corrections in candidate details such as name or photograph are generally not permitted at this stage . However, any discrepancies will be rectified at the time of counselling and document verification (DV), as per the examination guidelines. Candidates are advised to carry all relevant supporting documents during counselling/DV for verification.
Is it mandatory to carry a printed copy of the hall ticket?
What documents should I carry along with the hall ticket?
Candidates are advised to strictly follow the instructions mentioned in the admit card. Generally, candidates are required to carry:
1. A printed copy of the admit card (hall ticket)
2. A valid original Government-issued photo ID proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport, Voter-ID, DL, 10th Marksheet, etc.)
Ensure that the Name on ID proof and the Admit Card match.
Can I show the hall ticket on a mobile instead of a printout?

Candidates are advised to strictly follow the instructions mentioned in the admit card. Carrying a hard copy (printed copy) of the admit card is mandatory . Digital copies (such as on a mobile phone) will not be accepted at the examination center.
What is the reporting time for the exam?

Candidates are advised to strictly follow the reporting time mentioned in the admit card. It is recommended that candidates report to the examination center at least one hour before the commencement of the exam to ensure smooth entry and completion of all necessary formalities.
Will late entry be allowed?

Candidates are advised to strictly follow the reporting and entry timings mentioned in the admit card. Late entry is not permitted after the prescribed reporting time. Candidates must ensure timely arrival at the examination center to avoid any inconvenience.
How can I check my exam center location?

The exam center details are clearly mentioned in the admit card, including the full address of the allotted center. Candidates are advised to carefully review the admit card and follow the address mentioned for reporting at the examination center.
What items are prohibited inside the examination hall?
Candidates are advised to strictly follow the instructions mentioned in the admit card. The following items are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall:
1. Pen/ pencils, sheets, etc.
5. Any other electronic gadgets
Carrying any prohibited item may lead to disqualification or disciplinary action as per examination guidelines.
Can the exam center be changed after hall ticket release?

No, a change in the exam center is generally not permitted after the hall ticket has been released. However: Helpdesk teams should first understand the candidate's concern and attempt to address or resolve it through counselling or clarification. In exceptional or genuine cases, candidates may be advised to send a request email to nest-exam@niser.ac.in with:
Supporting documents
Detailed justification for the request
The final decision will be taken by the competent authority based on the merits of the case.

Disclaimer / Refund Policy

Refund Policy: No refund will be entertained for the exam fee once paid successfully (once for a particular application number). However, for any technical issues, if payment is received twice for the same application number, it will be refunded after the admission process is over. Please mention correct values of gender and reservation category in online application form which are the factors for finding the exam-fee to be paid. If at all wrong values were fed, then underpayment will reject your application and hence no admit card will be generated. However, applications with overpayment will be accepted without refund of the balance amount.
